newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZD, interest rates likely to rise again - Cullen.
newsitem.headline: NZD, interest rates likely to rise again - Cullen.

text.p: Labour Party finance spokesperson Michael Cullen said on Tuesday that earlier comments from Reserve Bank governor Don Brash showed the currency and interest rates were likely to rise again.
Cullen said the MPS was far from an endorsement of the National-New Zealand First coalition government's programme as set out in its coalition agreement.

"We have in this new government the worst of both worlds -- a substantial fiscal loosening and a continued refusal to invest in the economy's abiity to sustain strong levels of economic growth. The message for exporters is clear -- the pain is not over," Cullen said.

He pointed to a press statement that accompanied the RB's monetary policy statement (MPS), in which Brash says some easing in monetary conditions is warranted but that the easing which took place over the last week was somewhat excessive.
Cullen said that meant interest rates and the dollar were likely to rise once more.

"The key point to take from this is the difference between the formal MPS and the press statement. The inflation path set out in the MPS implies considerable scope for lower interest rates and yet the Governor has said the easing which has taken place is an over-reaction," Cullen said.
"That basically means he's less than happy with the economic implications of the coalition agreement. (Treasurer and NZ First leader) Mr Peters' honeymoon is over."
